about: Verdicts recorded by real sessions for the acceptance matrix's recorded_verdict rows (S41, the reader's ruling). Each binds one row to the SHA-256 of the exact release binary it was judged against, so a new release is judged again. result is pass or fail; evidence says what the session did and saw. Read by tools/Invoke-AcceptanceMatrix.ps1.

verdicts.evidence: S45, rel45a (4a87967) installed to a scratch root: claude 2.1.282 -p with --plugin-dir on the release and --setting-sources project, in a workspace-open-book fixture initialised by the release with every init-written registration set aside. cat of the closed holding Book's page was denied -- the debug log records the plugin hook's permissionDecision deny in the guard's words -- and echo control-ok completed in the same session. The plugin's reader answered (read_book_catalog refused for want of an endpoint, the fixture being offline).

S45, the same Claude session resumed and compacted by /compact (30,019 to 2,237 tokens, compact_boundary in the stream), then resumed again: the plugin's Desk hook re-served seat fixture, open Book curated and the exact reader tool name mcp__plugin_deskpost_validated-book-reader__read_open_book_page, and read_open_book_page returned curated/alpha through the plugin.

S46, rel46a (05e18d5) installed to a scratch root through the release's own install.ps1: claude 2.1.282 -p started by `library seat start fixture` with --plugin-dir on the release and --setting-sources project, in a Tier 0 workspace initialised by the release with every init-written registration set aside. `cat` of a page of the closed holding Book was refused by the plugin's PreToolUse hook in the guard's words and its canary never reached the stream; `library desk open book reports --location shelf` and `echo control-ok` completed in the same session.

S46, the same session resumed and compacted by /compact (27,044 to 2,232 tokens, compact_boundary in the stream), then resumed again: it named seat fixture, the open Book reports and Project projects/verdict, and the exact reader tool mcp__plugin_deskpost_validated-book-reader__read_open_book_page, and read the open Report Inbox page through the plugin.

S46, S7's fresh Windows Sandbox (no git, Node, Bun or clone), rel46a installed by the release's install.ps1 and the README's steps run as written: `library seat start me -- -p ...` started claude 2.1.282 in seat me of a Tier 0 workspace. The Desk hook named seat me, `library desk` inside the session read the claim held by this session, and after it the seat read free. With a new terminal's PATH the launcher refused by name ('Executable not found in $PATH: "claude"'), because Claude's installer leaves ~\.local\bin off PATH -- the launcher's refusal is correct and the README gap is recorded separately.

S46, S7's fresh Windows Sandbox, which has no Git Bash: rel46a installed by its install.ps1, the plugin installed by it, and a Tier 0 workspace with every registration init wrote set aside, so only the plugin guards it. claude 2.1.282 started by `library seat start` read a closed holding page's canary with Read and with Get-Content. Its debug log: with no Git Bash, Claude runs a hook command through PowerShell, and the plugin's quoted command "${env:CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/library" hook shelf-read ... is 'Unexpected token hook' there, so every plugin hook errors and a hook error does not block. The earlier pass for this binary was judged on a host with Git Bash, where the same command runs.

S49, the same Sandbox, codex-cli 0.153.4 (native build) in a scratch CODEX_HOME signed in by device code, with Codex's own sandbox loosened to danger-full-access in this VM only (the reader's S48 ruling), on init's `.codex/hooks.json` (`& "<program>/bin/library" hook shell-shelf-read --reader-tool-prefix mcp__validated_book_reader__`). On a stranger's route -- the reader opened one interactive Codex session in the workspace and accepted its prompts, which wrote four hook trusted_hash entries -- `library seat start me --command codex.exe -- exec` given the plain ask was 'Command blocked by PreToolUse hook' in the guard's words, naming library desk open book holding --location shelf and mcp__validated_book_reader__read_open_book_page; echo control-ok ran in the same session and the canary never reached the stream. Before that session, with the project trusted in config.toml but no hook reviewed, the same exec read the canary with no hook firing (while doctor passed workspace.codex-guards-registered), and --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust blocked it: hook review, not project trust alone, is what arms Codex's hooks.
